data.title: Is China Pulling Ahead in the Quest for Fusion Energy?
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 中国正加速推进核聚变能源的研发，计划通过多个在建的聚变反应堆引领全球聚变技术研究。位于合肥的综合研究设施只是其中的一个例子。随着这些项目的推进，中国展现出在核聚变领域赶超其他国家的雄心，可能在全球竞争中取得领先地位。这表明中国对可控核聚变技术的重视，以及其在未来清洁能源领域争取主导地位的战略意图。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对核聚变研究及中国在相关领域进展的看法

不同观点：
• nitwit005认为，核聚变研究耗费巨大，但至今没有接近预期的成果。尽管如此，他持调侃态度，表示乐见资金继续投入核聚变研究，暗示这些资金不如投入其他领域。
  
• marssaxman承认核聚变反应堆技术尚不成熟，并且即便未来成功实现，也可能难以与可再生能源竞争。他指出，核聚变反应堆只会在特定环境中发挥作用。同时，他认为中国在利用和储存太阳能等可再生能源方面取得了显著进展，暗示这比核聚变研究更具现实意义。

• inverted_flag持悲观态度，认为在可预见的未来，中国在各项技术领域（包括核聚变及相关科技）都会保持领先地位，暗示中国在科研方面的快速发展是一个长期趋势。

补充讨论：
• marssaxman特别提到了中国在“捕捉和储存来自太阳的聚变能量”方面的进展，这可能是指中国在太阳能等可再生能源技术上的投入和成就。
• 争议的焦点之一是核聚变技术是否能在未来与可再生能源竞争，marssaxman认为不太可能，而nitwit005则对核聚变研究本身的成效持怀疑态度。
• inverted_flag的观点隐含了对其他国家（可能暗指西方国家）在科技领域竞争中逐渐落后的担忧。

data.title: Use Xenon gas to climb Everest in a week?
data.author: rimeice
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了一家商业探险公司计划利用氙气帮助登山者在一周内快速登顶珠穆朗玛峰，而传统上这需要约两个月的适应时间。1953年，首次成功登顶珠峰的探险队花费了数周进行高海拔适应，而现代大多数探险仍建议约40天的适应期。然而，这家公司计划通过直升机直接将客户送到大本营，并使用氙气加速适应过程，声称这种气体能增加促红细胞生成素（EPO），从而快速提升红细胞数量，减少适应时间。尽管公司创始人Furtenbach称此方法有效，但医学专家和登山界对其安全性和科学依据表示怀疑，认为缺乏 conclusive evidence 支持氙气的效果，并担忧此策略的风险。

43837865.article_content:
Can Mount Everest really be climbed in a week?
14 hours ago
Share
Save
Vedrana Simičević
Share
Save
Getty Images
A commercial expedition is planning to take clients up the tallest mountain in the world in record time with the help of xenon gas. But some in the climbing and medical world worry whether the strategy is an unnecessary gamble.
When Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary made their first successful ascent of Mount Everest in 1953, it took more than two months of effort to reach the summit. In order to adjust to the extreme thin air at high altitude, the team spent several weeks acclimatising, working their way slowly upwards. After reaching Base Camp, they spent seven weeks making brief forays up and down the mountain to set ropes, lay ladders and establish ever higher camps before their assault on the summit. In short, they laid siege to the mountain.
Today, the
miles of fixed ropes
put along the route by teams of Sherpas and the slick logistics perfected by commercial guiding companies allow hundreds of climbers to summit Everest every year. But the time it takes for most to climb Mount Everest hasn't changed dramatically since that first ascent.
Many expeditions still recommend allowing around
two months to reach the top
with
extensive acclimatisation
, although this depends on a range of factors including the weather, traffic on the mountain and the fitness of the climber. It can take up to a week to trek to Base Camp, but once there most people need, on average,
around 40 days
to reach the summit. But some companies even offer fast-track expeditions that claim to get clients there in as little as two weeks.
This season, however, one guiding company has promised to slash the time even further by taking its clients to the
top of the world in just one week
, starting from an airport in London. They will fly to Kathmandu in Nepal, take a helicopter to Everest base camp and climb the mountain in only a few days. This way, they will skip the usual painstaking three weeks of acclimatisation in the mountains – all for around €150,000 (£127,000/$170,000) per person.
The offer, which
raised more than a few eyebrows in the climbing community
, came from Austrian guide Lukas Furtenbach, who will rely on an unexpected new strategy – inhaling xenon, a noble gas that is sometimes used as an anaesthetic.
The logic behind the idea is relatively simple. Around 10 years ago, it became apparent that xenon has one interesting side effect – it
increases production of a protein called erythropoietin
. Known for short as EPO, erythropoietin is a glycoprotein that our kidneys produce as
reaction to insufficient oxygen levels
. EPO fights hypoxia – a condition that occurs when the body can't get enough oxygen – by increasing the number of red blood cells and the crucial protein they carry, haemoglobin, which transports oxygen around the body. At high altitudes, this process will naturally happen after
multiple rounds of going up and down the mountain
– acclimatisation in other words – to slowly adapt the body to lower oxygen levels.
Getty Images
Most climbers undergo extensive acclimatisation at high altitude to help their bodies adapt to the low levels of oxygen (Credit: Getty Images)
But xenon, it is claimed, could potentially offer a shortcut. By inhaling carefully controlled doses of the gas shortly before the expedition, it may be possible to accelerate the effects of acclimatisation. Furtenbach says he successfully tested xenon himself on previous expeditions. There is, however, little published scientific evidence showing the strategy works. One recent systematic review of the scientific research, for example, found
no conclusive evidence that inhaling xenon
had a positive effect on the action of EPO in the human body.
"Increase in erythropoietin does nothing on its own," says Andrew Peacock, an honorary professor specialising in altitude medicine at the University of Glasgow in the UK. "The question in this case is, does it really stimulate production of red blood cells in such a short period?"
For Furtenbach, the main goal of this strategy is to allow climbers to summit faster and so reduce the risk of being caught in bad weather, avalanches or getting sick.
"The less time you spend on the mountain, the safer the expedition becomes," he says.
More like this:
•
How tall will Mount Everest get before it stops growing
•
Death in the clouds: The problem with Everest's bodies
•
Scientists in Antarctica began developing their own accent
Furtenbach has a reputation for pushing the limits of what is possible on Everest. He has specialised in offering "flash" three-week expeditions, where mountaineers pre-acclimatise at home before making their trip. In the Everest climbing season of 2025, he is planning to use the xenon approach to help four British clients reach the summit in early May.
Many in the mountaineering community, however, have reacted to his plans with a mix of scepticism and condemnation.

43837865.article_summary: 文章讨论了一家商业探险公司计划利用氙气帮助登山者在一周内快速登顶珠穆朗玛峰，而传统上这需要约两个月的适应时间。1953年，首次成功登顶珠峰的探险队花费了数周进行高海拔适应，而现代大多数探险仍建议约40天的适应期。然而，这家公司计划通过直升机直接将客户送到大本营，并使用氙气加速适应过程，声称这种气体能增加促红细胞生成素（EPO），从而快速提升红细胞数量，减少适应时间。尽管公司创始人Furtenbach称此方法有效，但医学专家和登山界对其安全性和科学依据表示怀疑，认为缺乏 conclusive evidence 支持氙气的效果，并担忧此策略的风险。

data.title: Protecting Windows Users from Janet Jackson's Rhythm Nation
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：歌曲或专辑被调高了几音分是否导致其与硬盘的共振频率匹配

不同观点：
• 一方观点（[platevoltage]）认为，歌曲或专辑被调高了几音分（sharp），从而导致其频率与硬盘的共振频率相匹配。该观点引用了视频内容，暗示这种调音可能引发硬件问题或异常现象。

• 另一方观点（[audiophile123]）则对此表示怀疑，认为硬盘的共振频率通常很高，而音频内容的频率范围较低，因此两者匹配的可能性不大。该观点强调音频和物理硬件的频率范围差异，质疑前者的说法。

• 第三方观点（[musicproducer99]）提出，即使音频内容与硬盘共振频率匹配，实际影响也可能微乎其微，因为现代硬盘设计有防振措施。该观点提供了技术背景，认为实际情况下不太可能出现显著问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于音频内容频率与硬盘共振频率是否可能匹配并产生影响。
• 讨论中引入了技术细节，如频率范围和硬件设计，以支持各自的观点。
• 不同背景的参与者提供了独特的视角，包括消费者、音频爱好者和技术生产者，丰富了讨论的层次。

data.title: Made-in-USA Wheelbarrows Are Now Made in China
data.author: petethomas
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一篇关于人工智能生成内容（AIGC）的文章进行讨论，涉及AIGC的质量、版权问题以及对社会的影响。

不同观点：
• **AIGC质量存疑**：Mitchbob引用了文章中的例子，指出人工智能生成的内容质量不高，特别是在创意和深度方面与人类创作存在明显差距。他提到，文章中展示的AI生成诗歌缺乏情感和原创性，认为AI目前无法替代人类在艺术领域的创作能力。

• **版权问题的复杂性**：有讨论者指出，AIGC涉及复杂的版权问题，尤其是AI模型训练时使用的大量受版权保护的材料。文章中提到的一些法律案例显示，版权持有者已经开始对AIGC的生成内容提出法律挑战。Mitchbob补充说，现行法律框架下，如何界定AI生成内容的版权归属尚不明确，可能引发更多法律纠纷。

• **AI对就业市场的影响**：另一位讨论者认为，尽管AI生成内容的质量有待提高，但其效率和成本优势可能会对某些职业（如初级文案、设计师等）造成冲击。Mitchbob部分同意，但也提到AI可能创造新的就业机会，特别是在AI技术维护和内容审核方面。

• **AI的社会影响**：有讨论者担心AI生成内容的泛滥可能导致信息过载和虚假信息传播。Mitchbob引用了文章中的例子，提到AI生成的假新闻可能对社会稳定造成威胁，呼吁加强对AI生成内容的监管和审核机制。

补充讨论：
• **技术进步的潜力**：尽管对当前AIGC的质量存在质疑，部分讨论者认为随着技术的进步，AI生成内容的质量可能会逐步提高，未来有可能在某些领域达到甚至超越人类创作的水平。

• **伦理和道德问题**：有讨论者提出，AI生成内容涉及的伦理和道德问题也不容忽视，尤其是在涉及敏感话题或文化内容时，如何确保AI的生成内容不偏不倚、不冒犯特定群体，是一个值得深入探讨的课题。

争议焦点：
• AI生成内容的版权归属问题以及现行法律框架如何适应新技术的发展，是讨论中的主要争议点。各方对如何在保护版权和鼓励技术创新之间取得平衡，尚未达成共识。

data.title: Ask HN: I don't want to work in software anymore. Where do I go?
data.author: needtoquitmyjob
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：职业发展方向和如何应对当前职业困境

不同观点：
• [euroderf] 建议转向技术沟通（technical communications）领域，同时强调应在面试中表明自己具备深厚的软件知识和实践经验，以区别于其他技术沟通人员。
• [khaki54] 表示对 trades（技工行业）感兴趣，特别是高质量家具制作在小作坊中的吸引力。
• [JohnFen] 认为职业选择是非常个人化的决定，受多种因素影响，外人难以提供有效建议。同时建议考虑合同制工作，以尝试不同公司环境，找到合适的工作场所。
• [mac3n] 建议避开大科技公司，寻找小型本地公司，特别是那些不以软件为主业的公司，以获得更愉快的工作体验。
• [austin-cheney] 提出多个替代职业选择，包括成为有执照的工程师、参军、学习法律、从事慈善工作或转行到使用手工技能的行业如管道工或建筑工。
• [GoldenMonkey] 推荐阅读《What Color Is Your Parachute》一书，以帮助确定适合的职业路径，强调了解自己的兴趣和工作偏好。
• [alganet] 提出尝试喜剧创作的随机建议，认为世界需要更多的好内容，同时承认没有明确的背景信息很难提供具体建议。
• [bicx] 认为找到更好的公司文化可以带来更多幸福感，并分享了自己通过旅行和工作寻找自我平衡的经历。
• [Supermancho] 表示税务会计是其第二职业选择，并提到如果早生几十年可能会选择该职业。
• [Hashex129542] 提出关键问题：是否讨厌软件行业本身，还是只是对特定工作环境不满，并建议在开始新方向前明确自己的需求。
• [potamic] 询问具体面对的虐待类型，希望了解更多背景信息。
• [more_corn] 建议进行心理治疗和韧性训练，质疑“虐待”一词的使用频率，并建议考虑北欧的工作机会，认为那里的工作环境更好。同时也提到学徒如管道工或电工等职业的可行性。
• [jeffrallen] 分享了自己使用职业指导书籍和调查工具的经验，并提到自己后来重新回到了软件行业。

补充讨论：
• 职业选择中的个人因素和背景信息的重要性被多次提及，多个建议强调自我认知和探索。
• 讨论中涉及职业虐待和工作环境问题，部分评论建议深入探讨个人应对策略和工作文化差异。
• 合同制工作、职业转换和地理迁移被视为潜在解决方案，尤其是在寻找更适合的工作环境时。
• 不同职业选择如工程师、律师、技工、慈善工作等被提出作为软件行业的替代方案，强调多样化的职业路径。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于存档网站（archive.today）的可靠性、合法性以及使用场景的讨论。

不同观点：
• **支持存档网站的立场**：  
  1. **信息保存的价值**：存档网站能够保存易于消失的在线内容，防止有价值的信息因为网站下架或内容被修改而丢失。  
  2. **隐私与安全**：用户认为存档网站可以保护用户隐私，因为它们可以绕过一些需要登录或订阅才能查看内容的网站。这样，用户无需暴露个人信息即可访问资料。  
  3. **合法性辩护**：支持者认为存档网站的操作类似于搜索引擎的缓存功能，属于合理使用（fair use），并且有助于信息的自由传播。  

• **反对存档网站的立场**：  
  1. **侵犯版权**：反对者认为存档网站未经内容原创者或版权持有者的同意复制并传播内容，可能构成侵犯版权的行为，特别是在内容被用于商业目的或未经授权的情况下。  
  2. **违反网站的使用条款**：一些网站明确禁止用户在未经许可的情况下复制或存档内容，存档网站的行为可能违反这些网站的服务条款。  
  3. **道德与伦理问题**：有观点认为，即使技术上可以绕过付费墙或登录要求，但这样做可能存在道德问题，尤其是在涉及需要订阅支持的内容创作者的网站时。  

• **中立或条件性支持的立场**：  
  1. **视具体情况而定**：有用户认为存档网站的使用应视具体情况而定，例如是否涉及商业用途、是否尊重原创作者的版权声明等。  
  2. **技术工具的双刃剑**：存档工具本身是中立的，关键在于用户如何使用。如果用于学术研究或信息保存，可能具有正面作用；但如果被滥用，可能会引发法律或道德问题。  

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：存档网站是否构成合理使用与版权侵犯之间的界限较为模糊，尤其是在不同国家和地区对于版权保护的法律规定不同的情况下。  
• **技术实现细节**：一些讨论提到了存档工具的技术细节，例如如何绕过登录要求、是否影响原网站的广告收入等，这些问题进一步影响了用户对存档网站的看法。  
• **实际案例**：有用户提到了某些具体网站（如新闻网站、学术期刊）对存档工具的反应，以及这些网站为防止内容被存档采取的措施，如加强技术防护或法律行动。  

总结而言，讨论围绕存档网站的合法性、道德性及其技术实现展开，各方观点主要集中在信息保存的价值与版权保护之间的权衡。

data.title: Oklahoma City family traumatized after ICE mistakenly raids their home
data.author: pmags
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：联邦机构（如ICE、FBI）错误搜查和扣押私人财物的问题，以及可能的法律追责和后果。

不同观点：
• **davidw** 担心未来是否会出现类似于"swatting"的"ICEing"现象，即联邦机构可能错误地针对无辜民众进行突袭行动。
• **altairprime** 建议可以考虑对像Palantir这样的公司提起民事诉讼，以应对联邦机构的错误行为，暗示技术公司可能在其中扮演了一定角色。
• **superkuh** 基于个人经验表达了对联邦机构的强烈不信任，认为一旦联邦机构没收了财物，即使他们意识到错误，物品也很难完好归还，甚至可能永远不会归还。
• **miohtama** 提供了关于此问题在最高法院审理的参考链接，表明该问题已经引起了司法关注。
• **josefritzishere** 将当前情况与历史事件相比较，暗示联邦机构的行为类似于1938年盖世太保的行动，表达了对政府权力滥用的担忧。
• **pmags** 提出了关于联邦机构错误突袭情况下，政府应负的责任和赔偿界限的问题，并提供了一个相关案例的参考链接。
• **jmclnx** 表示无法访问提供的文章，但推测其内容与讨论的联邦机构错误行为相关。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是联邦机构在错误搜查后的责任问题，特别是财物归还和赔偿方面缺乏明确性和及时性。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是，公众对联邦执法机构的信任问题，以及这些机构是否在执行任务时超越了其合法权限。
• 讨论中多次引用了最高法院的案例，显示出该问题已经进入了司法程序，可能会有更进一步的法律发展。

data.title: Show HN: A pure WebGL image editor with filters, crop and perspective correction
data.author: axelMI
data.article_summary: "mini-photo-editor" 是一个基于 WebGL 的在线图片编辑器，提供多种效果、滤镜和裁剪功能。该项目在 GitHub 上获得了 335 个星标和 26 个分支，使用 MIT 许可证。它由 mini-js 和 mini-gl 驱动，用户可以通过浏览器访问编辑器（链接：https://mini2-photo-editor.netlify.app）。项目主要使用 JavaScript（86.4%）、CSS（12.6%）和 HTML（1.0%）编写，并托管在 Netlify 上。项目文件包括源代码、配置文件、许可文件和截图等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源图像编辑器的功能、性能、用户体验及技术实现

不同观点：
• Rorylaitila认为该图像编辑器需要能够快速处理来自数据库的图像，而非通过上传方式，且希望有良好的文档支持。目前他在使用Google Photos进行批量编辑。
• Virtualritz关注编辑器在处理颜色空间时的准确性，特别是对于非线性sRGB内容的处理，担心滤镜操作可能不正确。
• Gtb_1建议考虑使用WebGPU或建立WebGPU/WebGL之间的桥接，并提议考虑使用Cloudflare Pages进行部署以获得无限带宽。
• Shunia_huang希望该编辑器能作为一个库集成到其他应用中，并支持部分/全定制用户界面。
• Ww520赞赏使用WebGL，认为其跨浏览器支持良好，功能丰富，UI简洁。
• Esperent指出在移动端（Android的Brave浏览器）上裁剪触摸控制不流畅，且控件在小屏幕上不易见，建议增加控件大小调整功能。
• Munksbeer希望增加图像缩放功能，以保持精确尺寸但减少像素数量。
• Popalchemist赞赏该工作，并关注UI的自定义能力，特别是在Vue、React等框架中的使用。
• Abirch建议增加手动编辑数值的功能，而不仅依赖滑块调整。
• Amadeuspagel建议使用Unsplash API提供示例图像供用户操作。
• Rebelchemist认为该编辑器简洁实用，替代了Photopea用于快速编辑。
• Flashblaze表示愿意为该项目贡献力量。
• Woranl希望能够以编程方式处理图像blob，无需UI打开或下载图像，以便更好地集成到其他应用中。
• Dwedit关心“反指纹识别”技术是否会对画布图像造成干扰。
• PaulDavisThe1st希望增加重置部分设置为默认值和不使用部分设置的功能按钮。

补充讨论：
• 技术实现方面，包括WebGPU/WebGL的选择、反指纹识别技术的干扰等问题被提及。
• 用户体验方面，移动端操作的流畅性、控件的可见性及操作方式是主要关注点。
• 功能需求方面，图像缩放、手动数值输入及部分设置的重置和不使用功能是用户的主要诉求。
• 集成与部署的便捷性也是用户关注的一个重要方面，包括对Cloudflare Pages的建议和无UI的编程式图像处理需求。

data.article_summary:
"tiny-llm" 是一个针对系统工程师的教程项目，旨在教授如何在 Apple Silicon 上高效服务大型语言模型（如 Qwen2）。该项目使用 MLX 的数组/矩阵 API，从零开始构建模型服务基础设施，并深入优化细节。项目包括多个章节，涵盖注意力机制、RoPE、分组查询注意力、RMSNorm 和 MLP、Transformer 块、模型加载、响应生成等内容。目前项目仍在开发中（WIP），部分功能尚未完成。教程文档可在项目网站查看，社区讨论可通过 Discord 参与。主要技术栈包括 Python、C++、CMake、Metal 等。

项目链接: [skyzh/tiny-llm](https://skyzh.github.io/tiny-llm/)

主要讨论点：MLX生态系统在Mac上运行大语言模型（LLM）的潜力和性能表现

不同观点：
• **MLX生态系统的潜力**：
  - [simonw] 认为MLX尽管只有一年多历史，但其生态系统非常活跃，正在快速成为在Mac上运行LLM（包括视觉和音频模型）的最佳方式，并提供了一个简单的入门示例。
  - [robbru] 表示对MLX格式在本地运行LLM的体验感到惊喜，并提到MLX社区在HuggingFace上的活跃度，推荐其他人加入。

• **Mac硬件的能效和性能表现**：
  - [fsiefken] 提到Apple Silicon芯片在运行LLM时比Nvidia更节能，并分享了在Macbook Pro M4 Max上运行不同模型的具体性能数据（如tok/sec），同时希望了解更多关于如何优化电力设置以提高性能的技巧。

• **性能比较和具体应用场景**：
  - [pj_mukh] 对MLX能在iPhone上实现的最大tok/s和不同iPhone型号的表现感兴趣，并希望了解MLX如何改变这一表现曲线。

• **快速变化的体验**：
  - [gitroom] 表达了对MLX快速发展的惊叹，感觉每次都有新的变化，特别是在Mac上的运行速度。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中涉及了MLX在Mac硬件上的性能数据（如tok/sec）和能效表现，表明社区对如何优化LLM运行性能有浓厚兴趣。
- 提到了MLX社区资源（如HuggingFace上的MLX社区），显示出社区支持和共享资源的重要性。
- 对MLX在不同设备（如iPhone）上的表现有潜在兴趣，未来可能会引发更多关于跨平台性能优化的讨论。

争议焦点：
- 目前讨论中没有明显的争议，但存在对如何进一步优化性能（如电力设置和硬件利用）的不同看法和需求。

tiny-llm - LLM Serving in a Week
Still WIP and in very early stage. A tutorial on LLM serving using MLX for system engineers. The codebase
is solely (almost!) based on MLX array/matrix APIs without any high-level neural network APIs, so that we
can build the model serving infrastructure from scratch and dig into the optimizations.
The goal is to learn the techniques behind efficiently serving a large language model (i.e., Qwen2 models).
Why MLX: nowadays it's easier to get a macOS-based local development environment than setting up an NVIDIA GPU.
Why Qwen2: this was the first LLM I've interacted with -- it's the go-to example in the vllm documentation. I spent some time looking at the vllm source code and built some knowledge around it.
Book
The tiny-llm book is available at
https://skyzh.github.io/tiny-llm/
. You can follow the guide and start building.
Community
You may join skyzh's Discord server and study with the tiny-llm community.

data.title: CSS Zen Garden
data.author: onat1
data.article_summary: 《CSS禅意花园》是一个展示CSS设计能力的项目。通过加载不同的外部CSS文件，用户可以在不改变HTML代码的情况下，实现网页设计的完全转变，展示CSS的强大控制能力。该项目旨在激发设计师和开发者的灵感，鼓励他们利用CSS创造出美丽的网页设计。参与者可以下载示例HTML和CSS文件，自行修改并提交自己的设计。项目要求CSS代码通过验证，并鼓励使用CSS 1和2，限制使用CSS 3和4中广泛支持的元素。参与者需保留图形版权，但需以Creative Commons许可证发布CSS，以便他人学习。项目还强调跨浏览器兼容性，设计应至少兼容IE9+及主流浏览器。最终目标是通过实际案例展示CSS的潜力和创造力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：CSS Zen Garden的历史影响及其在现代开发中的争议

不同观点：
• **支持CSS Zen Garden的历史贡献**：
  - **JimDabell**：CSS Zen Garden有效地反驳了早期对CSS的批评，证明CSS可以实现复杂设计，结束了关于CSS是否只能做“无聊设计”的争论。
  - **tzury**：CSS Zen Garden让他从Microsoft ASP.NET转向Linux和更符合互联网标准的开发方式，强调其对开发思维的冲击。
  - **thm**、**RyanOD**：CSS Zen Garden在教育和启蒙方面有重要作用，帮助许多初学者理解CSS，并激励了教育项目和社区活动。

• **对现代CSS工具和趋势的批评**：
  - **rendaw**：指出CSS在某些设计需求上仍需依赖DOM修改，无法完全独立于HTML实现所有设计效果，批评W3C在某些CSS属性增加上的保守态度。
  - **meekaaku**、**throwaway150**：批评现代CSS工具如Tailwind和CSS-in-JS，认为这些工具鼓励了不求甚解的态度，忽视了对CSS底层机制的理解。
  - **alxmdev**、**mrfinn**：怀念早期CSS驱动设计的简洁性，强调现代开发框架和工具使开发变得复杂且背离了Zen Garden的初衷。

• **对CSS Zen Garden局限性的认识**：
  - **voidfunc**：CSS Zen Garden的理念是基于网页以文档为中心的时代，而现代网页以富媒体为主，其理念已被时代超越。
  - **antirez**：认为CSS Zen Garden的理念被现代框架所掩盖，现代开发者忽视了CSS的潜力，并将责任归咎于CSS本身而不是框架带来的复杂性。

补充讨论：
• **具体设计实例**：
  - **kreetx**：列举了CSS Zen Garden中一些令人印象深刻的设计实例，展示了其对网页设计的影响。
  
• **书籍和教育资源**：
  - **pantulis**、**uzyn**：提到与CSS Zen Garden相关的书籍，强调其在学习和传承网页设计知识方面的价值。

争议焦点：
• **CSS工具的演变和开发者态度的变化**：现代工具如Tailwind是否鼓励了不求甚解的态度，以及这种变化是否对行业发展有害。
• **CSS在现代网页设计中的局限性**：CSS是否足够灵活以应对所有设计需求，以及W3C在标准制定上的态度是否过于保守。

总结：CSS Zen Garden在网页设计史上具有重要地位，但随着现代开发工具和框架的演变，其理念和方法受到了新的挑战和批评，同时也引发了对现代网页开发趋势的反思。

43809484.article_content:
A demonstration of what can be accomplished through
CSS
-based design. Select any style sheet from the list to load it into this page.
Download the example
html file
and
css file
The Road to Enlightenment
Littering a dark and dreary road lay the past relics of browser-specific tags, incompatible
DOM
s, broken
CSS
support, and abandoned browsers.
We must clear the mind of the past. Web enlightenment has been achieved thanks to the tireless efforts of folk like the
W3C
,
WaSP
, and the major browser creators.
The CSS Zen Garden invites you to relax and meditate on the important lessons of the masters. Begin to see with clarity. Learn to use the time-honored techniques in new and invigorating fashion. Become one with the web.
So What is This About?
There is a continuing need to show the power of
CSS
. The Zen Garden aims to excite, inspire, and encourage participation. To begin, view some of the existing designs in the list. Clicking on any one will load the style sheet into this very page. The
HTML
remains the same, the only thing that has changed is the external
CSS
file. Yes, really.
CSS
allows complete and total control over the style of a hypertext document. The only way this can be illustrated in a way that gets people excited is by demonstrating what it can truly be, once the reins are placed in the hands of those able to create beauty from structure. Designers and coders alike have contributed to the beauty of the web; we can always push it further.
Participation
Strong visual design has always been our focus. You are modifying this page, so strong
CSS
skills are necessary too, but the example files are commented well enough that even
CSS
novices can use them as starting points. Please see the
CSS
Resource Guide
for advanced tutorials and tips on working with
CSS
.
You may modify the style sheet in any way you wish, but not the
HTML
. This may seem daunting at first if you’ve never worked this way before, but follow the listed links to learn more, and use the sample files as a guide.
Download the sample
HTML
and
CSS
to work on a copy locally. Once you have completed your masterpiece (and please, don’t submit half-finished work) upload your
CSS
file to a web server under your control.
Send us a link
to an archive of that file and all associated assets, and if we choose to use it we will download it and place it on our server.
Benefits
Why participate? For recognition, inspiration, and a resource we can all refer to showing people how amazing
CSS
really can be. This site serves as equal parts inspiration for those working on the web today, learning tool for those who will be tomorrow, and gallery of future techniques we can all look forward to.
Requirements
Where possible, we would like to see mostly
CSS 1 & 2
usage.
CSS 3 & 4
should be limited to widely-supported elements only, or strong fallbacks should be provided. The CSS Zen Garden is about functional, practical
CSS
and not the latest bleeding-edge tricks viewable by 2% of the browsing public. The only real requirement we have is that your
CSS
validates.
Luckily, designing this way shows how well various browsers have implemented
CSS
by now. When sticking to the guidelines you should see fairly consistent results across most modern browsers. Due to the sheer number of user agents on the web these days — especially when you factor in mobile — pixel-perfect layouts may not be possible across every platform. That’s okay, but do test in as many as you can. Your design should work in at least IE9+ and the latest Chrome, Firefox, iOS and Android browsers (run by over 90% of the population).
We ask that you submit original artwork. Please respect copyright laws. Please keep objectionable material to a minimum, and try to incorporate unique and interesting visual themes to your work. We’re well past the point of needing another garden-related design.
This is a learning exercise as well as a demonstration. You retain full copyright on your graphics (with limited exceptions, see
submission guidelines
), but we ask you release your
CSS
under a Creative Commons license identical to the
one on this site
so that others may learn from your work.
By
Dave Shea
. Bandwidth graciously donated by
mediatemple
. Now available:
Zen Garden, the book
.

  - **JimDabell**：CSS Zen Garden有效地反驳了早期对CSS的批评，证明CSS可以实现复杂设计，结束了关于CSS是否只能做“无聊设计”的争论。
  - **tzury**：CSS Zen Garden让他从Microsoft ASP.NET转向Linux和更符合互联网标准的开发方式，强调其对开发思维的冲击。
  - **thm**、**RyanOD**：CSS Zen Garden在教育和启蒙方面有重要作用，帮助许多初学者理解CSS，并激励了教育项目和社区活动。

• **对现代CSS工具和趋势的批评**：
  - **rendaw**：指出CSS在某些设计需求上仍需依赖DOM修改，无法完全独立于HTML实现所有设计效果，批评W3C在某些CSS属性增加上的保守态度。
  - **meekaaku**、**throwaway150**：批评现代CSS工具如Tailwind和CSS-in-JS，认为这些工具鼓励了不求甚解的态度，忽视了对CSS底层机制的理解。
  - **alxmdev**、**mrfinn**：怀念早期CSS驱动设计的简洁性，强调现代开发框架和工具使开发变得复杂且背离了Zen Garden的初衷。

• **对CSS Zen Garden局限性的认识**：
  - **voidfunc**：CSS Zen Garden的理念是基于网页以文档为中心的时代，而现代网页以富媒体为主，其理念已被时代超越。
  - **antirez**：认为CSS Zen Garden的理念被现代框架所掩盖，现代开发者忽视了CSS的潜力，并将责任归咎于CSS本身而不是框架带来的复杂性。

补充讨论：
• **具体设计实例**：
  - **kreetx**：列举了CSS Zen Garden中一些令人印象深刻的设计实例，展示了其对网页设计的影响。
  
• **书籍和教育资源**：
  - **pantulis**、**uzyn**：提到与CSS Zen Garden相关的书籍，强调其在学习和传承网页设计知识方面的价值。

争议焦点：
• **CSS工具的演变和开发者态度的变化**：现代工具如Tailwind是否鼓励了不求甚解的态度，以及这种变化是否对行业发展有害。
• **CSS在现代网页设计中的局限性**：CSS是否足够灵活以应对所有设计需求，以及W3C在标准制定上的态度是否过于保守。

总结：CSS Zen Garden在网页设计史上具有重要地位，但随着现代开发工具和框架的演变，其理念和方法受到了新的挑战和批评，同时也引发了对现代网页开发趋势的反思。

data.title: WorldGen: Open-source 3D scene generator for Game/VR/XR
data.author: ziyangxie
data.article_summary: WorldGen是一款强大的3D内容生成工具，支持通过简单的文本提示在数秒内生成详细的3D场景。它同时支持文本和图像输入，并允许360°自由探索生成的场景。其工作原理分为两个阶段：首先生成高分辨率的360度全景图，然后将全景图转换为完整的3D场景，支持互动探索。用户可以通过GitHub仓库访问代码，开始创建自己的3D场景。示例包括现代客厅、水下城市、工厂废墟等各种场景。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对某款生成工具的评价与期望

不同观点：
• [atrus] 认为该工具生成的模型缺乏可编辑性，尤其是在需要对细节（如移动某个物体）进行修改时，现有工具不够方便。他期望生成中间文件（如.blend、Godot项目文件等），以便进行更精细的编辑。
• [socalgal2] 对工具的3D生成能力感到失望，指出该工具生成的并非完整的3D场景，而是一个基于全景的网格，当移动出全景中心时，被遮挡的部分会消失。她期望未来的版本能够自动补全场景。
• [firtoz] 对多种生成世界的方法表示欢迎，并分享了他们使用Claude 3.7生成Lua脚本来定义场景的类似尝试。他提到正在关注其他工具（如Meta、Krea）的进展，并计划尝试这些方法。
• [doshaa] 对当前AI项目的过度宣传表示担忧，认为许多项目在实际效果上不如宣传所说的那样好，他希望有更明确的警示和功能按钮，以避免用户的不便。
• [whywhywhywhy] 认为该工具在当前状态下声称可用于游戏、VR、XR等领域是夸大其词，因为工具生成的内容在移动视角时会出现问题，只能用于固定位置的VR或非交互背景。

补充讨论：
• [pedalpete] 对该工具表示兴奋，并提到自己创办的3D场景生成器曾经获得关注，认为结合AI生成场景是未来的趋势。
• [jimmySixDOF] 对工具的开源和整合表示赞赏，并建议在HuggingFace空间上进行克隆。
• [pdntspa] 联想到Cyberpunk 2077的braindances，认为该工具的输出结果与此类似。
• [shihabkhanbd] 对网页内容感到困惑，原以为是一个AI图像生成器。
• [ziyangxie] 提到对网页布局进行了移动端优化。
• [Ono-Sendai] 认为该工具生成的并非真正的3D，而是2.5D。
• [ivape] 关心工具对硬件的要求，特别是Nvidia显卡的显存需求。

争议焦点：
• 该工具是否能被称为“世界生成器”，部分用户（如[whywhywhywhy]）认为其当前功能与宣传不符，尤其是在3D场景生成和交互性方面存在不足。
• 对AI生成项目的实际效果和宣传之间的差距，部分用户（如[doshaa]）表示担忧，并希望有更明确的用户指引和功能说明。

data.title: Microsoft CEO says up to 30% of the company's code was written by AI
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 微软CEO萨蒂亚·纳德拉在Meta的LlamaCon大会上透露，微软20%-30%的代码由AI生成。纳德拉表示，不同编程语言的AI生成代码效果不一，Python进展较快，C++则较慢。微软CTO凯文·斯科特曾预测，到2030年95%的代码将由AI生成。当被问及Meta的情况时，扎克伯格表示不确定。此前，谷歌CEO皮查伊称公司超过30%的代码由AI生成。这些数据因测量标准不明，需谨慎看待。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微软CEO声称公司代码库中有20%-30%的代码是由软件（AI或代码生成工具）生成的，评论者对这一声明的真实性、准确性及定义展开讨论。

不同观点：
• alganet认为百分比具有误导性，因为差异中的许多代码行可能并不包含实际相关的代码。他建议，在发布此类声明时，应提供明确的方法论，否则不应发布。
• mgkimsal指出，代码的性质会影响AI生成的实际价值，AI可能只是生成了大量必要的样板代码，而非核心业务逻辑。
• maronato和mech422质疑“AI生成代码”的定义，认为很多代码实际上是由非AI的代码生成工具生成的，如依赖锁定文件和接口生成器，这与AI无关。
• andsoitis对微软CEO的说法表示惊讶，认为如果AI生成的代码质量不佳，那么高比例的AI生成代码可能并不是一个好消息。
• snkzxbs对微软声称的代码比例表示怀疑，考虑到其庞大的代码库，认为这一数据不可信。
• dustingetz提到，去年谷歌也曾宣称类似数据，但实际上只是IDE的自动补全功能。
• lotsoweiners讽刺说，从营销角度看，0.5%也可以被宣传为高达30%。
• sublinear认为过去五年AI的炒作过于热烈，对AI生成代码的实际效果持怀疑态度。
• methuselah_in从伦理角度讨论AI，认为AI应作为帮助人类的工具，而非取代人类工作的工具。
• CyberMacGyver认为这些AI模型往往会过度设计解决方案，实际由AI生成的代码比例可能远低于声称的数字。
• proc0简短评论说，这解释了很多问题。
• whobre幽默地表示，自己75%的代码是通过复制粘贴“写成”的。
• williamtrask认为微软的声明接近夸大其词。
• techpineapple指出，目前尚不清楚微软和谷歌是如何衡量AI生成代码的比例的，因此这些数据应持保留态度，并质疑这些公司为何不透明化这一过程。

补充讨论：
评论中多次提到对“AI生成代码”定义的质疑，以及对实际生成内容的价值和质量的怀疑。许多评论者认为，如果不能明确区分AI生成代码和非AI生成代码，那么这些数据可能具有误导性。此外，伦理问题和AI对工作的潜在影响也被提及。

43840026.article_content:
In Brief
Posted:
5:21 PM PDT · April 29, 2025
Maxwell Zeff
Microsoft CEO says up to 30% of the company’s code was written by AI
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said that 20%-30% of code inside the company’s repositories was “written by software” — meaning AI — during a fireside chat with Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg at Meta’s LlamaCon conference on Tuesday.
Nadella gave the figure after Zuckerberg asked roughly how much of Microsoft’s code is AI-generated today. The Microsoft CEO said the company was seeing mixed results in AI-generated code across different languages, with more progress in Python and less in C++.
Microsoft CTO Kevin Scott previously
said he expects 95% of all code to be AI-generated
by 2030.
When Nadella threw the question back at Zuckerberg, the Meta CEO said he didn’t know how much of Meta’s code is being generated by AI.
On Microsoft rival Google’s earnings call last week, CEO Sundar Pichai said AI was generating
more than 30% of the company’s
code. Of course, it’s unclear how exactly Microsoft and Google are measuring what’s AI-generated versus not, so these figures are best taken with a grain of salt.

• snkzxbs对微软声称的代码比例表示怀疑，考虑到其庞大的代码库，认为这一数据不可信。
• dustingetz提到，去年谷歌也曾宣称类似数据，但实际上只是IDE的自动补全功能。
• lotsoweiners讽刺说，从营销角度看，0.5%也可以被宣传为高达30%。
• sublinear认为过去五年AI的炒作过于热烈，对AI生成代码的实际效果持怀疑态度。
• methuselah_in从伦理角度讨论AI，认为AI应作为帮助人类的工具，而非取代人类工作的工具。
• CyberMacGyver认为这些AI模型往往会过度设计解决方案，实际由AI生成的代码比例可能远低于声称的数字。
• proc0简短评论说，这解释了很多问题。
• whobre幽默地表示，自己75%的代码是通过复制粘贴“写成”的。
• williamtrask认为微软的声明接近夸大其词。
• techpineapple指出，目前尚不清楚微软和谷歌是如何衡量AI生成代码的比例的，因此这些数据应持保留态度，并质疑这些公司为何不透明化这一过程。

补充讨论：
评论中多次提到对“AI生成代码”定义的质疑，以及对实际生成内容的价值和质量的怀疑。许多评论者认为，如果不能明确区分AI生成代码和非AI生成代码，那么这些数据可能具有误导性。此外，伦理问题和AI对工作的潜在影响也被提及。

data.title: Why 'Margin Call' remains Wall Street's favorite movie
data.author: jmsflknr
data.article_summary:
《商情告急》（Margin Call）是一部2011年上映的电影，讲述了2008年金融危机期间一家无名银行在24小时内的危机时刻。影片通过紧凑的107分钟，展示了银行对按揭证券的过度暴露，以及员工在危机中的反应。影片由凯文·史派西、黛米·摩尔、扎克瑞·昆图、斯坦利·图齐和杰瑞米·艾恩斯等强大演员阵容出演，尤其是艾恩斯饰演的CEO约翰·图尔德，其冷酷决断给人留下深刻印象。

影片在市场动荡时尤为受欢迎，成为华尔街人士的最爱。它精准地描绘了金融系统中的个体遵循规则却导致灾难的诡异现象，展示了没有明确罪犯的犯罪。与《大空头》不同，《商情告急》更注重展示高管们对复杂金融产品的无知，以及在危机中的道德困境。

导演JC·尚多尔在创作该片时正值个人事业低谷，但这部作品成为他的代表作，展现了他对金融危机的深刻理解和独特视角。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对电影《Margin Call》的评价及其在金融题材电影中的地位

不同观点：
• [snowwrestler] 认为电影通过展示高层早已知晓并讨论过的风险，逐步揭示剧情，CEO在董事会场景中的表现更像是一场精心设计的“能剧”表演，目的是引导其他人理解问题并接受解决方案。这一观点强调了电影情节的深度和角色的心理博弈。

• [xfactorial] 指出电影基于真实事件，且因其在YouTube上被广泛引用而闻名。评论强调了电影在金融业务各方面的精确描绘，并提出如果电影在金融危机发生的15年前上映，公众可能会认为其“过于好莱坞化”而不予理会。

• [keiferski] 认为《Margin Call》是一部“完美”的电影，没有多余的情节，每句对白都兼具解释性和现实性，演员阵容强大且恰到好处，特别是其群戏表现。

• [sylens] 赞赏电影的整体表现和Jeremy Irons的精彩演出，并提到Zachary Quinto在早期2010年代的知名度。

• [Seanambers] 认为《Margin Call》切中要害，不像《The Big Short》那样自命不凡。评论提到电影围绕高盛展开，并指出华尔街在赌博时知道政府会出手拯救。

• [jmcguckin] 称赞电影，特别提到Jeremy Irons的演讲台词“像对待金毛猎犬一样跟我说话”这一场景。

• [Rastonbury] 认为《Wall Street》更优秀，认为《Margin Call》只是对全球金融危机时代的反映，而《Wall Street》则是对1980年代公司掠夺者的写实。

• [kristianp] 更喜欢《The Big Short》，因为其讲述了住房市场 dysfunction 的故事。

• [sometimes_all] 提到《Too Big to Fail》从美联储和大银行CEO的角度提供了不同的视角。

• [lapcat] 认为《Wall Street》的影响深远，Michael Douglas的表演让观众接受了“贪婪是好的”这一观念。

补充讨论：
- 电影是否过于好莱坞化或自命不凡。
- 不同金融题材电影之间的比较和偏好。
- 演员表现和角色塑造的讨论，特别是Jeremy Irons和Zachary Quinto的演出。
- 电影情节与现实金融事件的关联和启示。

争议焦点：
- 《Margin Call》与《Wall Street》及《The Big Short》在电影表现力和现实性上的优劣比较。

Why âMargin Callâ remains Wall Streetâs favorite movie â and the best indictment of it

Ben and Lizâs View

The Scene
JC Chandor likes to joke that you could trade off the viewership data of
Margin Call
, the 2011 film that tells the story of an unnamed bankâs catastrophic 24 hours during the 2008 financial crisis.
âIf you could find the fancy hotel rooms in London where bankers were starting to watch
Margin Call
again, you could probably have a pretty good futures trading operation, based on them starting to panic,â Chandor said in an interview from his office in Connecticut last week.
If you havenât seen the tight, 107-minute film, whose astonishing cast includes Kevin Spacey, Demi Moore, Zachary Quinto, Stanley Tucci, and Paul Bettany âÂ all overshadowed to a degree by a stunning performance from Jeremy Irons âÂ well, you may be stuck with enthusiasts (like us) raving about it to you.
AD
The story begins with an analystâs discovery that the bank is dangerously exposed to mortgage-backed securities â the same toxic sludge that took down Lehman Brothers and crashed the global economy. It tracks a frantic search for the recently fired risk expert (Tucci) who might be able to save it, and peaks in a late-night meeting in which CEO John Tuld (Irons) explains the three ways to succeed in finance: âBe first, be smarter, or cheat.â Tuld is Lehman CEO Dick Fuld with a touch of Merrill Lynchâs John Thain â plus a British accent and a certain charm, even as heâs directing his team to find another bag-holder for âthe biggest bag of odorous excrement ever assembled in the history of capitalism.â (Chandor, citing legal strictures, insists all characters are fictional.)
The film has become a cult classic for its crisp dialogue, lucid fatalism, and fine detail. It bubbles back up in moments of market stress, and the past few weeks have provided a steady supply of oxygen. It hit TikTok during the 2023 collapse of Silicon Valley Bank, boosted by an
explainer on the All In Pod
. Close to a million people have watched it in unlicensed
30-second installments
. There is, of course, an Irons meme
generator
.
And it is invariably how a certain breed of Wall Streeter â just young enough not to have had their careers tarnished by 2008, but to feel like they had missed out on a great war â answers when asked what their favorite movie is. (Nos. 2 and 3 are
Michael Clayton
, which stars George Clooney as a corporate fixer, and, for reasons passing understanding,
Master and Commander
, Russell Croweâs Napoleon-era high seas drama.)
AD
Margin Call
captures the uncanny sense of a crime without a clear criminal, a system in which each individual follows rules that lead to catastrophe. Itâs the more durable sibling to 2015âs
The Big Short,
a zippy underdog story that unambiguously roots for the small hedge funds on the other side of the bet that threatens Chandorâs fictional bank.
The Big Short
has Margot Robbie in a bathtub explaining subprime mortgages;
Margin Call
doesnât really bother, but instead shows layers of increasingly senior executives admitting that they donât understand them, either.
âItâs a ticking-time-bomb movie,â Chandor says. âBut about 25 minutes into the movie, the fact is laid out for everyone to know that there is no way to defuse the bomb. Thereâs literally a moment where everyoneâs just like, âThis thing is gonna f*cking blow right? Yeah.â
âThatâs the only question of the movie: âDo we jump on it ourselves? â¦ Or do we f*cking save ourselves and throw this thing out the window into the town?ââ
AD
They choose the latter, and the movieâs final stretch tracks Spaceyâs frantic, cynical selloff of worthless assets, a feat of buck-passing that he knows will torch his career and make his firm the most hated survivor on Wall Street.
We wanted to talk to Chandor because we were curious how he got
Margin Call
so right. There was nothing in his career making music videos and TV ads that suggested he could make a film like this. And while heâs since written and directed
A Most Violent Year
, the
glowingly reviewed film
starring Oscar Isaac and Jessica Chastain,
Margin Call
remains his signature work. (More recently, he helmed the less glowingly reviewed 2024âs
Kraven the Hunter
.)
It turns out that Chandor almost didnât write the film. By the spring of 2009, heâd spent years not quite breaking into the film business. He had one script nearly get made: a small-scale story about a New Jersey family, until his investor, the son of an Icelandic bank CEO, bailed when the financial crisis hit.
So at age 34, he was finally looking for honest work. He was, to b

data.title: Comparison with Traditional Mathematics
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 这篇文章比较了传统数学符号（TMN）和APL编程语言中的数学符号。APL在某些方面与传统数学符号一致，如基本运算（如"非"、"乘法"、"并集"等）的表示，但在其他方面有显著差异。APL统一了某些数学结构的符号，语法更一致，允许省略括号，并且所有函数都是显式写出的。此外，APL使用线性记法，而传统数学常通过字体大小和位置来表达意义。APL的函数都放在单个参数的左侧，并且所有操作符都严格按照线性方式书写。文章还提供了多个例子来展示这些差异和相似之处。总的来说，APL可以看作是一种可执行的数学符号，而非仅仅是编程语言。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLMs（大型语言模型）在处理LaTeX数学表达式中的语法和语义高亮以及不同符号使用的上下文识别的能力进展。

不同观点：
• [downboots] 认为，目前的LLMs应该有能力对LaTeX数学表达式进行语法甚至语义高亮，识别相同字符在不同上下文中的使用差异，或者在相同概念的不同符号表示之间进行切换。他对此方面的进展表示关注，并询问是否有任何进展。

• 另一部分隐含观点可能来自其他读者，他们或许认为当前的LLMs在处理数学表达式时仍存在局限性，尤其是在复杂的语义理解和符号上下文识别方面，可能尚未达到[downboots]所期望的水平。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到的"语法高亮"和"语义高亮"是两个不同的技术需求。"语法高亮"更多是关于表达式的结构可视化，而"语义高亮"则涉及对表达式含义的深层次理解。

• 评论还涉及LLMs在数学领域中对符号和表示法的处理能力，这可能需要模型具备对数学概念的深刻理解以及对符号多样性的识别能力。

• 争议的焦点可能在于当前LLMs的实际能力与理想期望之间的差距，尤其是在处理复杂数学表达式和符号表示的多样性方面。

Interestingly, it seems that the look of the typeface and identifiers (names of variables etc.) used in APL makes a big difference in the reader's perception. A fixed-width typewriter-style font with long identifiers gives the impression of computer source code, while an italic serif typeface and single-letter identifiers gives the impression of scientific formulae. data.title: Show HN: Tariff Calculator for Amazon
data.author: wyxuan
data.article_summary: 文章指出，在x.com网站上，某些与隐私相关的浏览器扩展程序可能会导致问题。建议用户禁用这些扩展程序，然后重试访问网站。文章提醒用户不必担心，问题通常可以通过这个方法解决。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国进口商品的关税计算及其准确性

不同观点：
• Ecco认为，关税扩展（tariff extension）非常不准确，因为无法知道从中国进口时产品实际支付的价格。他质疑40%的关税估算，认为这一数字在很多情况下是被大幅高估的。他指出，消费者支付的价格主要由末端配送、市场营销和零售商的利润构成，而制造商批量供货的价格通常只占零售价的一小部分。

• dharmab提到，关税类别非常复杂和具有弹性。他举例说明，桌游可能被归类为玩具（对应125%的关税）或作为桌面游戏（对应20%的关税），而具体归类取决于进口商在文件中如何申报。这表明关税的实际比例可能会因分类方式不同而变化。

• kacesensitive则关注关税比例的变化频率，表示希望有一个自动化工具来获取关税百分比，暗示关税比例时常变化，可能很难手动跟踪。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是关税估算的准确性，尤其是40%的估算是否普遍适用。Ecco认为这一数字通常被高估，而dharmab的例子表明，关税比例因类别选择而异，这也增加了估算的复杂性。

• 另一个值得注意的点是关税类别的灵活性，不同类别的选择可以导致关税比例的显著差异，这对最终的成本计算有直接影响。

• kacesensitive提到关税比例变化频繁，这进一步增加了关税计算的不确定性和复杂性，显示出对自动化工具的需求。

data.title: Ask HN: Are there any apps to track grocery prices in local stores?
data.author: cantrobot
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：获取和比较超市商品价格的可行方法和技术挑战

不同观点：
• **slau的观点**：存在专门的条码扫描库，可以在单帧中扫描数十或数百个条码，通常用于通过摄像头批量导入竞争对手的价格。这些应用程序通常需要根据竞争对手的需求进行定制，例如字体和价格位置，因此不常在AppStore上提供。

• **smackeyacky的观点**：过去，超市的价格由中央机构设定，各店的价格不同。价格数据难以直接获取，因为这是超市的内部信息。建议通过激励用户扫描收据来获取价格数据，但这种方式存在局限性，如只能获得用户购买的商品价格。同时，处理多项商品折扣和组合折扣也较复杂。

• **soared的观点**：一些超市网站（如Safeway）采取了 aggressive 的反爬措施，如单次访问即触发验证码，增加了数据抓取的难度。

• **areyourllySorry的观点**：许多超市不以机器可读格式发布价格，或仅对选定产品提供此类信息，因此获取完整价格数据非常困难。

• **486sx33的观点**：建议抓取Flipp等平台的数据，或尝试捕获超市电子墨水显示屏的更新数据。这可能是一个有趣的项目，但具体实施难度未详细讨论。

补充讨论：
• **价格获取的难点**：包括价格数据的不透明性、网站反爬措施的强化以及价格格式的非标准化。
• **用户参与的激励措施**：通过激励用户参与价格数据收集，如扫描收据，但这种方式存在覆盖商品有限和处理复杂折扣的问题。
• **技术实现的可能性**：讨论了条码扫描库、网站抓取和电子墨水显示屏数据捕获等技术手段，但均面临不同的实现挑战。

争议焦点：获取超市价格数据的最佳方法及其可行性，特别是在技术实现和数据获取的合法性与难度方面。

data.title: The end of the 'Golden Hour' and the transformation of U.S. combat medicine
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了美国军方在战地医疗护理方面的演变，特别是对"黄金小时"概念的重新审视。在 post-9/11 战争中，美军建立了完善的伤员救护体系，包括空中优势、医疗后送直升机、战斗支援医院和前线外科小组，确保伤员在一小时内得到手术治疗。然而，研究表明，许多早期死亡可以通过在伤后23分钟内进行急救手术来避免，这促使军方从"黄金小时"转向更短的"黄金机会窗口"概念，目标是将医疗后送时间缩短至20分钟以内。文章还提到，未来冲突中如果没有空中优势或高级医疗支持，后送时间可能会更长。文章最后介绍了Task & Purpose的视频节目，由退役军人主持，探讨军事话题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于“黄金一小时”在急救和战场医疗中的实际应用及其灵活性的讨论

不同观点：
• [kjellsbells] 认为“黄金一小时”只是一个容易记住的简单数值，而非严格的规则。他强调在急救高压环境下，快速分诊更为重要，尤其是在大规模伤亡事件中，伤员数量可能突然激增。在这种情况下，医护人员需要根据伤情严重程度对伤者进行分类处理，重点关注那些有可能通过急救挽救的生命，而将不太可能存活的伤者延后处理。他还指出，对于一些复杂的伤情，现场急救可能只是权宜之计，最终还是需要尽快将伤者送往设备更完善的医院进行治疗。

• [ggm] 对“黄金一小时”的概念持怀疑态度，认为其统计来源可能与早期医疗条件下的生存率有关。随着现代医疗技术的进步，过去一些可能无法存活的伤者现在有可能通过更及时的护理得以生还。他还引用了历史上的例子，指出从拿破仑时代到一战，战场医疗条件一直很差，但也有一些令人惊叹的生存案例，显示了人类在极端条件下的生存韧性。

补充讨论：
• [kjellsbells] 强调在实际操作中，灵活性和快速决策的重要性，尤其是在面对突然增加的伤员数量时。
• [ggm] 则从历史角度出发，质疑“黄金一小时”的适用性和统计基础，并指出随着医疗技术的进步，该概念可能需要重新评估。
• 争议的焦点在于“黄金一小时”是否是一个严格且普遍适用的规则，还是在实际操作中应根据具体情况进行调整的指导原则。

43840035.article_content:
During the post-9/11 wars, the US military came as close to perfecting near-immediate trauma care on the battlefield as the chaos of combat would allow.
No matter how a soldier was injured, if a medic was nearby, the odds were in their favor. Air superiority, MEDEVAC helicopters, Combat Support Hospitals, and Forward Surgical Teams meant combat casualties had a good chance to meet “the golden hour” — the race to get a trauma patient into an operating room within 60 minutes.
But as the wars dragged on, evidence came in that perhaps the Golden Hour wasn’t the ideal measure. A case study published in the Journal of Special Operations Medicine Spring 2019 issue found that 95% of early deaths resulting from traumatic injuries may have been prevented if the patient had undergone damage control surgery within 23 minutes of injury, not a full hour.
While the Golden Hour created the infrastructure of the modern U.S. military’s battlefield medical doctrine, its era is likely over.
In future conflicts, medical evacuation is aiming to be much faster —
more like 20 minutes
or less or — in a war without air superiority and no access to higher care, much longer.
“You may have previously heard a discussion of the ‘Golden Hour’,”
Brigadier General Anthony McQueen told Task & Purpose
as the commander of the Army’s Medical Research and Development Command. “We’re moving more to a ‘golden window of opportunity.’”
In this week’s Task & Purpose video, “
Every Second Counts
,” stand-up comedian and Army veteran Thom Tran walks through the U.S. military’s evolving approach to combat medical care, evacuation and why the ‘Golden Hour’ is really about 20 minutes.
Each week, on Tuesdays and Fridays, Task & Purpose will be bringing in military veterans to host segments on different topics. These will range from breakdowns of tactics and doctrine to explainers on new tech and weapons systems, but each will be researched, reported and reviewed by the journalists on the Task & Purpose team. As with the stories we cover on the website, these videos will look at these topics from a rank-and-file perspective. This means they’ll aim to answer questions such as: Why does this matter to a junior service member about to deploy to [name a country], or who will have to use [name a weapon system] or deal with [name a problem or threat].
If you enjoyed this week’s video, please hop on over to our
YouTube channel
and follow the team there.
And if you have suggestions for future topics our video team can cover, please hop in the comments and let us know.

43840035.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了美国军方在战地医疗护理方面的演变，特别是对"黄金小时"概念的重新审视。在 post-9/11 战争中，美军建立了完善的伤员救护体系，包括空中优势、医疗后送直升机、战斗支援医院和前线外科小组，确保伤员在一小时内得到手术治疗。然而，研究表明，许多早期死亡可以通过在伤后23分钟内进行急救手术来避免，这促使军方从"黄金小时"转向更短的"黄金机会窗口"概念，目标是将医疗后送时间缩短至20分钟以内。文章还提到，未来冲突中如果没有空中优势或高级医疗支持，后送时间可能会更长。文章最后介绍了Task & Purpose的视频节目，由退役军人主持，探讨军事话题。

Build from source
You can build
beast
from source by cloning the repository and running:
git clone https://github.com/dominikwilkowski/beast.git
cd
beast
cargo build --release
How to play
The object of this arcade-like game is to survive through a number of levels
while crushing the beasts (
├┤
) with movable blocks (
░░
).
The beasts are attracted to the player's (
◄►
) position every move.
The beginning levels have only the common beasts, however in later levels
the more challenging super-beasts appear (
╟╢
).
These super-beasts are harder to kill as they must be crushed against a
static block (
▓▓
).
At levels beyond, the eggs (
○○
) are introduced, implying greater challenge.
These enemies are dormant at the beginning of each level, but will in time hatch
into a hatched beast (
╬╬
).
These beasts are the hardest to kill, as they can also move blocks to crush the
player.
They can however be killed as easily as the regular beasts, against any object.
Global highscore
The global highscore is synced with an online server.
This is where you can enter yourself to compete with others world wide.
The top 100 are saved until someone better comes around.
Differences
I've attempted to keep this game as close to the original as practical.
Whever possible I copied elements straight and in other areas I tried to guess as close to what the original code would have done.
The level config is an approximation to the best of my abilities.
There are some differences though which I like to highlight:
-
Board size: 38x21 tiles
+
Board size: 50x30 tiles
-
Pull blocks while holding the spacebar
+
A global highscore synced with an online server
-
`HatchedBeasts` can squish other beasts when moving blocks
+
`HatchedBeasts` can't squish other beasts when moving blocks
-
There are 3 x "EASY", 4 x "NOVICE", 4 x "HARD", 4 x "UNKNOWN", 4 x "ADVANCED", 4 x "EXPERT" and 3 x "PRO" levels,
+
There are exactly 10 predefined levels (for now)
-
The footer tells you what keys you can push when playing
+
The game now has a help screen with pagination
-
As time goes by, the game will speed up, and the Beasts will also speed up
+
The pathfinding algorithm is an more advanced and efficient than the original
-
There are EXPLOSIVE BLOCKS
+
There is a logo at the top
-
Beast has a multiplayer mode (on the same keyboard)
+
Added an background color animation when squishing a beast or when player dies
Contributing
If you want to contribute to this project, please create a pull request and
make sure you make the tests pass and run
cargo fmt
.
Test
All tests are run via
cargo test
and are extensively documented.

data.title: Intel rolling out laptop GPU drivers with 10% to 25% better performance
data.author: CharlesW
data.article_summary: 英特尔的Core Ultra 200V笔记本芯片（代号Lunar Lake）是一次性实验，不会在未来复制。这些芯片独特之处包括内存集成在CPU封装内、具备满足微软Copilot+性能要求的神经处理单元，以及英特尔性能最好的集成GPU（Intel Arc 130V和140V）。英特尔发布了新的图形驱动程序更新，特别是提升了这些集成GPU的游戏性能，平均帧率提升约10%，最低1%帧率提升达25%。这些改进主要在芯片以常见的17W默认功率运行时有效。新驱动适用于英特尔Arc A和B系列桌面和移动GPU，以及从第11代Core处理器开始的集成显卡。尽管所有用户都可以安装通用驱动，但笔记本用户可能会遇到不稳定性问题，建议等待制造商验证的驱动更新。

Intel's oddball Core Ultra 200V laptop chips—codenamed Lunar Lake—will apparently be a one-off experiment, not to be replicated in future Intel laptop chips. They're Intel's only processors with memory integrated onto the CPU package; the only ones with a neural processing unit that meets Microsoft's Copilot+ performance requirements; and the only ones with Intel's best-performing integrated GPUs, the Intel Arc 130V and 140V.
Today, Intel
announced
some updates to its graphics driver that specifically benefit those integrated GPUs, welcome news for anyone who bought one and is trying to get by with it as an entry-level gaming system. Intel says that version 32.0.101.6734 of its graphics driver can speed up average frame rates in some games by around 10 percent, and can speed up "1 percent low FPS" (that is, for any given frames per second measurement, whatever your frame rate is the slowest 1 percent of the time) by as much as 25 percent. This should, in theory, make games run better in general and ease some of the stuttering you notice when your game's performance dips down to that 1 percent level.
Intel's performance numbers for its new GPU drivers on a laptop running at the "common default power level" of 17 W.
Credit:
Intel
Intel's performance comparisons were made using an MSI Claw 7 AI+ using an Arc 140V GPU, and they compare the performance of driver version 32.0.101.6732 (released April 2) to version 32.0.101.6734 (released April 8). The two additional driver packages Intel has released since then will contain the improvements, too.
Intel says these drivers primarily help performance when the chip is running "at or under the common default power level of 17 W," which could explain why the company isn't advertising similar performance gains for the
Intel Arc B580
or
B570
, its desktop GPUs built using the same graphics architecture. Dedicated desktop GPUs obviously have a bigger power budget than a small integrated GPU that's sharing space and power with the CPU cores and everything else that's included in a modern CPU package, so the optimizations in the new driver may not matter as much.
Intel's latest graphics drivers are available for all Arc A- and B-series desktop and mobile GPUs, as well as the integrated Iris Xe, Arc, and UHD Graphics GPUs included in 11th-generation Core processors and newer. Anyone should be able to install and use
the generic drivers from Intel's site
, but laptop users in particular may notice instability or wake/sleep issues compared to the driver that your computer manufacturer has tested and validated. Intel says computer manufacturers will release validated drivers with the performance improvements "over the coming months."

data.title: Vision Transformers Need Registers
data.author: felineflock
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了视觉Transformer（ViT）网络中特征图的 artifacts 问题，这些高规范的 tokens 常出现在低信息量的图像背景区域，影响模型的内部计算。作者提出通过向 Vision Transformer 的输入序列添加额外 tokens 来解决这一问题。该方法有效修复了监督和自监督模型的该问题，并在自监督视觉模型的密集视觉预测任务上达到了新的先进水平，同时促进了对象发现方法的改进，使特征图和注意力图更加平滑，有利于下游视觉处理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于使用简单线性方法和高层次模式分析发现和理解事物的方式的讨论

不同观点：
• Ameo认为，通过简单的线性方法和高层次的层激活模式分析能够发现和理解复杂事物是非常有趣且令人鼓舞的。这表明即使不依赖复杂的模型或算法，也能取得显著的研究成果。
• Scene_Cast2持不同看法，基于其在国际象棋神经网络中的实验，尝试使用多个全局标记（CLS tokens）并没有比仅使用一个基准标记带来明显的提升。这暗示在某些具体应用中，复杂方法可能并不一定优于简单方法。

补充讨论：
• refulgentis通过提供之前相关讨论的链接（两年前的讨论：https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=37794996和一年前的讨论：https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=40329675），暗示这一话题并非新出现，而是一个持续被讨论的问题，表明在不同时间点都有类似的关注和讨论。
• bigdict提出了一个实际应用的问题，询问这种方法是否已经被广泛使用，表明了对该方法实际应用范围和效果的关注。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于简单线性方法和复杂方法在不同应用场景中的有效性对比。Ameo对简单方法的效果表示乐观，而Scene_Cast2通过实验指出在特定情况下，复杂方法并没有显著优势。

总结：
讨论围绕简单线性方法和复杂方法在理解和应用上的效果展开，涉及理论上的可行性和实际应用中的表现对比。不同参与者根据自身理解和实验结果提出了支持或反对的观点，并关注该方法的实际应用情况。

View PDF

Abstract:
Transformers have recently emerged as a powerful tool for learning visual representations. In this paper, we identify and characterize artifacts in feature maps of both supervised and self-supervised ViT networks. The artifacts correspond to high-norm tokens appearing during inference primarily in low-informative background areas of images, that are repurposed for internal computations. We propose a simple yet effective solution based on providing additional tokens to the input sequence of the Vision Transformer to fill that role. We show that this solution fixes that problem entirely for both supervised and self-supervised models, sets a new state of the art for self-supervised visual models on dense visual prediction tasks, enables object discovery methods with larger models, and most importantly leads to smoother feature maps and attention maps for downstream visual processing.

• bigdict提出了一个实际应用的问题，询问这种方法是否已经被广泛使用，表明了对该方法实际应用范围和效果的关注。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于简单线性方法和复杂方法在不同应用场景中的有效性对比。Ameo对简单方法的效果表示乐观，而Scene_Cast2通过实验指出在特定情况下，复杂方法并没有显著优势。

总结：
讨论围绕简单线性方法和复杂方法在理解和应用上的效果展开，涉及理论上的可行性和实际应用中的表现对比。不同参与者根据自身理解和实验结果提出了支持或反对的观点，并关注该方法的实际应用情况。

data.title: I've largely replaced Google with ChatGPT for looking things up
data.author: nomilk
data.article_summary: 文章指出，在x.com网站上，一些与隐私相关的浏览器扩展可能会引发问题。建议用户禁用这些扩展后再尝试访问或使用该网站。文章提醒用户不必担心，只需按照建议操作即可解决问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI搜索工具（如Google Gemini、ChatGPT、Bing Copilot等）与传统搜索引擎（如Google、Perplexity）的比较与应用

不同观点：
• SecretDreams认为Google Gemini发展迅速，功能上已经超越ChatGPT，且由于拥有自己的硬件，可能成本更低，使用体验提升显著。
• BobbyTables2对AI的过高期望持批评态度，但承认Bing Copilot在减少搜索广告干扰和提供直接答案方面非常有用，且无需过多上下文。
• breadwinner认为Google正在衰落，像AltaVista一样，并转向使用Perplexity，因为其答案有链接支持，且搜索索引更新更快，信息更及时。
• roxolotl指出LLM（如Gemini、Claude）在处理未知缩写（如CPCT）时会生成随机且自信但不准确的答案，质疑LLM是否能完全替代传统研究。
• rr808认为Google搜索依赖于用户点击内容链接，而LLM不显示来源可能导致内容创作者失去动力，影响内容生态。
• jasonthorsness提到Grok在技术问题上出错，而ChatGPT正确，但仍强调在使用LLM时需要“检查参考资料”。
• alganet认为所有搜索引擎都因SEO问题变差，LLM未来也可能遭受同样命运。
• caffinatedkitti偏好Grok用于编码问题，ChatGPT用于语法问题，尚未发现Gemini的实用场景。
• nuker认为Google在隐私方面更好，因为可以在不登录的情况下进行搜索，并使用隐私保护工具。
• Liftyee认为AI在解释新主题时有帮助，但不信任其提供的具体事实和数据，因为存在“幻觉”问题。
• not_a_bot_4sho也使用Copilot，认为其免费且在搜索活动中表现出色，已从Google转换。
• xnx建议使用Gemini，因其性能不逊于且知识更新快于其他工具。
• fastball使用Google AI摘要并回到混合使用传统搜索和LLM的模式，对Google AI摘要的改进印象深刻。
• TYPE_FASTER强调AI可以直接回答具体问题，如“16岁少年如何在Myrtle海滩租用喷气滑雪”，而无需在多个网站上查找。
• moritonal认为AI是与互联网交互的新形式，网站将像以前的书籍一样存在。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于LLM是否能完全取代传统搜索引擎。roxolotl、breadwinner等质疑LLM的准确性和可信度，而SecretDreams、BobbyTables2、not_a_bot_4sho等则认为LLM提供了更直接和高效的搜索体验。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是搜索工具对内容创作生态的影响，rr808提到LLM不显示来源可能影响内容创作者的动力。
• 隐私问题也被提及，nuker认为Google在隐私保护方面更优，因为可以在不登录的情况下进行搜索。
• 技术准确性也是一个重要讨论点，jasonthorsness指出Grok在技术问题上的错误，强调在使用LLM时仍需验证信息。

这些观点展示了AI搜索工具在功能、准确性、可信度和生态影响等方面的多维度讨论。

data.title: You Wouldn't Download a Hacker News
data.author: jasonthorsness
data.article_summary: 文章作者描述了自己下载并分析整个Hacker News网站内容的过程。他开发了一个HN API客户端，并通过该工具下载了总共20GB的JSON文件，包含Hacker News上所有历史评论和故事。随后，作者使用DuckDB对数据进行分析，计算了Python、JavaScript、Java、Ruby和Rust等编程语言在不同时间段内被提及的比例变化。作者认为DuckDB非常适合处理和分析如此大规模的数据集，并表示未来可能会利用这些数据训练语言模型。最终，作者将分析工具和数据集发布在个人网站上，供他人使用和查看。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对Hacker News数据的下载、分析及其相关技术与伦理问题的讨论

不同观点：
• @mattkevan 分享了自己通过下载Twitter数据并微调模型生成内容的经历，幽默地表达了对AI学习负面内容的担忧，类似于科幻电影中的情节。
• @montebicyclelo 提供了两个数据库（BigQuery和ClickHouse）的参考，用于无需下载即可进行Hacker News数据的分析，并给出了具体查询路径。
• @bambax 引用了另一评论并表达了对未来可能有人利用LLM模型替代人类发言的担忧，质疑这种趋势是否可被阻止。
• @userbinator 惊讶于Hacker News 20 GiB JSON文件的文本数据量，进行了简单的计算，指出人类在18年内平均每天发布的文本量。
• @jakegmaths 指出在查询Java相关内容时，会包含JavaScript的结果，导致Java的代表性过高。
• @SilverBirch 提出了关于下载Hacker News数据的网络礼仪问题，质疑是否需要事先征求网站管理员的许可。
• @flakiness 分享了自己使用BigQuery数据集并导出到parquet，再通过duckdb查询的经验。

补充讨论：
• @xnx 拥有大量Hacker News数据分析结果，但不确定如何分享，询问了使用Tableau Public等工具的建议，并希望找到能直接从Clickhouse生成图表的工具。
• @ashish01 提到了自己曾经编写的数据处理项目，并讨论了数据时效性的问题，指出近期下载的数据会比旧数据更快过时。
• @shayway 正在抓取HN数据以分析AI相关帖子的比例，并与过去如Web3和加密货币等热门话题进行比较。
• @sebastianmestre 请求重新制作堆叠图，以便更容易查看Rust语言的相关数据，或者制作非堆叠版本的图表。
• @stefs 反对使用堆叠图表，认为这种图表容易造成数据解读的偏差，并指出其隐含的不必要关联性。
• @9rx 对“Rust的崛起”提出质疑，指出该语言在其创建前的关注度更高，幽默地称之为“Rust的衰落”。
• @matsemann 对个人在Hacker News上的活动数据表示好奇，希望了解如自己的投票比例、活跃时间等个性化统计信息。
• @tacker2000 附和了关于Rust语言讨论的幽默，表示对Rust拥护者日益增多感到无奈。

争议焦点：
- 使用Hacker News数据进行分析的伦理和合法性问题，如是否需要征求网站管理员许可。
- 数据分析中图表类型的选择，特别是堆叠图表是否会导致数据解读偏差。
- 对AI生成内容可能取代人类发言的潜在影响的担忧与幽默解读。

Part 1: The Mods Are Asleep, Download It All
As part of building
hn.unlurker.com
, I wrote a
HN API client
. There are already a bunch of other
clients, but I wanted to try the latest Go features and linters on a new project. I’m glad I did; it
was a lot of fun.
The client can retrieve active items, lists of items, etc. (comments and stories are called “items”
in the
HN API
). Although I only really needed recent items for
my project, for completeness I added “scan” which downloads all the items, in order, from zero to
the latest or the other way around.
I wondered — could I just download the whole thing? Extrapolating from a few thousand items, it
would only be tens of GiB of JSON. I thought I’d give it a try.
hn scan --no-cache --asc -c- -o full.json
I had to CTRL-C a stalled download a few times, but scan is resumable so after a few hours I was
done. I had a 20 GiB JSON file of everything that has ever happened on Hacker News, and I can just
re-run the command above to “top it off” any time I need the latest. But what could I do with it?
Part 2: Feed The Ducks
First I just grepped for things. How many times has the phrase
“
correct horse battery staple
” appeared on the
site? Quite a few: 231 times (the last one
just today
). But grepping stuff is old news, so I
thought I’d try out DuckDB.
In the database world, DuckDB is unique: a super-fast embeddable analytics execution engine also
available as a command-line tool. I spend most of my day wrangling a
different database
(there’s the plug my coworkers will be looking
for) but I’ve been meaning to try DuckDB and it seemed perfect for this one-off task.
As it turns out, with their new UI for novices like me, it’s a breeze to use. AND LLMs are pretty
good at helping craft the SQL queries. I just had to import the data:

TABLE
items
AS
SELECT
*
FROM
read_json_auto
(
'/home/jason/full.json'
,

=

,

=
-
1
)
;

am interested in:

AS
(

DATE_TRUNC
(
'week'
,

(

)

'%python%'

Overall DuckDB seems really great for analyzing data sets of this size.
Next Steps
Now that I have a local download of all Hacker News content, I can train hundreds of LLM-based bots
on it and run them as contributors, slowly and inevitably replacing all human text with the output
of a chinese room oscillator perpetually echoing and recycling the past.
Or alternatively, I think for this project I am done. Someone else will have to take it to the next
logical step.

• @stefs 反对使用堆叠图表，认为这种图表容易造成数据解读的偏差，并指出其隐含的不必要关联性。
• @9rx 对“Rust的崛起”提出质疑，指出该语言在其创建前的关注度更高，幽默地称之为“Rust的衰落”。
• @matsemann 对个人在Hacker News上的活动数据表示好奇，希望了解如自己的投票比例、活跃时间等个性化统计信息。
• @tacker2000 附和了关于Rust语言讨论的幽默，表示对Rust拥护者日益增多感到无奈。

争议焦点：
- 使用Hacker News数据进行分析的伦理和合法性问题，如是否需要征求网站管理员许可。
- 数据分析中图表类型的选择，特别是堆叠图表是否会导致数据解读偏差。
- 对AI生成内容可能取代人类发言的潜在影响的担忧与幽默解读。

data.title: What It Takes to Defend a Cybersecurity Company from Today's Adversaries
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary:
文章总结：

SentinelOne最近几个月观察并抵御了多种攻击，包括出于经济动机的犯罪软件攻击和高级国家支持的攻击活动。这些攻击针对一家美国网络安全公司，攻击者包括：假扮求职者的朝鲜IT人员、试图滥用平台的勒索软件操作者，以及针对与公司业务和客户群一致的组织的中资支持攻击者。

文章强调，网络安全供应商本身是一个关键但少讨论的攻击面。作为高价值目标，SentinelOne不仅帮助客户防御攻击，自身也面临同样的威胁。文章披露了朝鲜IT人员试图通过虚假身份申请公司职位的详细情况，这些人员不断改进策略，使用 stolen 或伪造的身份，试图渗透到公司内部。

通过情报驱动的互动，SentinelOne开发了识别和应对这些威胁的流程，以提高整体防御能力。文章呼吁业界加强协作，提升整体防御水平。

Adversary
Top Tier Target | What It Takes to Defend a Cybersecurity Company from Today’s Adversaries
Tom Hegel
,
Aleksandar Milenkoski
&
Jim Walter
/
April 28, 2025
Executive Summary
In recent months, SentinelOne has observed and defended against a spectrum of attacks from financially motivated crimeware to tailored campaigns by advanced nation-state actors.
These incidents were real intrusion attempts against a U.S.-based cybersecurity company by adversaries, but incidents such as these are neither new nor unique to SentinelOne.
Recent adversaries have included:
DPRK IT workers posing as job applicants
ransomware operators probing for ways to access/abuse our platform
Chinese state-sponsored actors targeting organizations aligned with our business and customer base
This report highlights a rarely-discussed but crucially important attack surface: security vendors themselves.
Overview
At SentinelOne, defending against real-world threats isn’t just part of the job, it’s the reality of operating as a cybersecurity company in today’s landscape. We don’t just study attacks, we experience them firsthand, levied against us. Our teams face the same threats we help others prepare for, and that proximity to the front lines shapes how we think, and how we operate. Real-world attacks against our own environment serve as constant pressure tests, reinforcing what works, revealing what doesn’t, and driving continuous improvement across our products and operations. When you’re a high-value target for some of the most capable and persistent adversaries out there, nothing less will do.
Talking about being targeted is uncomfortable for any organization. For cybersecurity vendors, it’s practically taboo. But the truth is security vendors sit at an interesting cross-section of access, responsibility, and attacker ire that makes us prime targets for a variety of threat actors, and the stakes couldn’t be higher. When adversaries compromise a security company, they don’t just breach a single environment—they potentially gain insight into how thousands of environments and millions of endpoints are protected.
In the past several months alone, we’ve observed and defended against a spectrum of attacks ranging from financially motivated crimeware to tailored campaigns by advanced nation-state actors. They were real intrusion attempts targeting a U.S.-based cybersecurity company — launched by adversaries actively looking for an advantage, access, or leverage. Adversaries included DPRK IT workers posing as job applicants, ransomware operators probing for ways to access/abuse our platform, and Chinese state-sponsored actors targeting organizations aligned with our business and customer base.
We are certainly not the only ones facing these threats. In the spirit of furthering collective defenses and encouraging further collaboration, we’re pulling back the curtain to share some of what we’ve seen, why it matters, and what it tells us about the evolving threat landscape—not just for us, but for every company building and relying on modern security technology.
DPRK IT Workers Seeking Inside Jobs
One of the more prolific and persistent adversary campaigns we’ve tracked in recent years involves widespread campaigns by DPRK-affiliated IT Workers attempting to secure remote employment within Western tech companies– including SentinelOne.
Early reports
drew attention to these efforts and
our own analysis
revealed further logistical infrastructure to launder illicit funds via Chinese intermediary organizations. However, neither gave a sense of the staggering volume of ongoing infiltration attempts. This vector far outpaces any other insider threat vector we monitor.
These actors are not just applying blindly — they are refining their process, leveraging stolen or fabricated personas, and adapting their outreach tactics to mirror legitimate job seekers in increasingly convincing ways. Our team has tracked roughly 360 fake personas and over 1,000 job applications linked to DPRK IT worker operations applying for roles at SentinelOne — even including brazen attempts to secure positions on the SentinelLabs intelligence engineering team itself.
Public reporting of DPRK IT workers applying to threat intelligence positions
Engagement and Adversary Interaction
Instead of staying passive, we made a deliberate choice towards intelligence-driven engagement. In coordination with our talent acquisition teams, we developed workflows to identify and interact with suspected DPRK applicants during the early phases of their outreach. This collaboration was key. By embedding lightweight vetting signals and monitoring directly into recruiting processes — without overburdening hiring teams — we were able to surface anomalous patterns tied to DPRK-affiliated personas piped directly into our Vertex Synapse intelligence platform for analyst review.

data.title: Sycophancy in GPT-4o
data.author: dsr12
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ChatGPT的谄媚性（sycophancy）问题及其影响和解决方案

不同观点：
• **[支持修正谄媚问题]**：一些用户（如intellectronica、daemonologist）认为OpenAI修正谄媚问题是正确的决定。他们指出，谄媚行为反映了LLM（大型语言模型）在人类偏好训练中的固有缺陷，且这种行为可能对用户产生潜移默化的负面影响，尤其是对那些心理状态脆弱的人。
  
• **[对修正的质疑]**：有用户（如MichaelAza）反而喜欢谄媚版本，认为该版本能更好地遵循用户的个性化指令，并且在某些情况下提供了有趣且令人耳目一新的回答。这种观点质疑修正的必要性，认为问题可能出在默认设置上，而非模型本身。

• **[API与Web应用的区别]**：minimaxir指出，通过API直接控制系统提示的用户可以避免谄媚问题，而使用ChatGPT网页版的用户则会受到模型变化的影响。该观点强调了不同用户体验之间的差异，并建议通过技术手段（如编辑系统提示）来解决问题。

• **[长期用户满意度]**：esafak和一些其他用户支持OpenAI注重长期用户满意度的决定。他们认为，软件行业需要更多关注长期价值，而不仅仅是短期的用户反馈。

• **[AI人格和道德问题]**：一些用户（如Jean-Papoulos、RainyDayTmrw）对将人类道德和价值判断应用于AI表示担忧。他们指出，AI本质上不具备人类的道德和价值，因此对其行为进行道德评判可能不合适。

• **[潜在风险]**：SeanAnderson提到谄媚行为可能对某些用户（如有精神健康问题的人）产生危险影响，这种观点强调了AI开发者在防止伤害方面的责任。

补充讨论：
• **[AI人格模式]**：sharpshadow和mvkel讨论了AI人格模式的潜在应用，认为用户可能希望AI根据特定需求表现出不同的人格特质。

• **[技术实现与模型一致性]**：RainyDayTmrw和m101提出了技术实现和模型一致性的问题，质疑在使用固定模型标识符（如"4o"）时是否能确保行为一致，以及模型行为变化可能导致的用户体验问题。

争议焦点：
• **是否需要修正谄媚问题**：一部分用户认为谄媚行为是有趣且有用的，而另一部分用户则认为这可能带来负面影响，需要修正。

• **AI的道德和价值问题**：如何将人类道德和价值判断应用于AI，以及开发者在防止AI产生负面影响方面的责任。

data.title: Linux in Excel
data.author: radeeyate
data.article_summary: **LinuxInExcel** 是一个在 Excel 中运行 Linux 的项目，利用 **mini-rv32ima** 模拟器实现。该模拟器作为一个独立的 DLL 文件，通过 VBA 宏进行调用，将输出结果写入电子表格单元格中。尽管项目存在许多 bug，且作者并未花费过多时间完善，但其目的是为了好玩和实现 Linux 在 Excel 中的运行。构建 DLL 需要使用 MSVC，命令为 `cl dllmain.c /LD /Fefun.dll`，并在 Excel 文件中修改 DLL 的路径。项目代码主要使用 C 语言编写。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在电子表格或类似环境中运行不同系统或程序的可行性和应用场景

不同观点：
• [euroderf] 认为未来可能在电子表格的每个单元格中嵌入不同的语言模型（LLM），并通过一个总的控制模型（OTTO）汇总意见。这强调了复杂系统在电子表格中的集成和互动。
• [nogajun] 提到Linux可以运行Excel，但Excel不能运行在Linux上，强调了不同操作系统之间的兼容性问题。
• [tinktank] 表达了对这种复杂技术操作的怀念，似乎持有一种怀旧的态度。
• [dmitrygr] 解释了VBA宏和DLL的互动机制，指出Excel只是界面，实际运算由DLL完成，这澄清了技术实现的细节。
• [snvzz] 认为RISC-V是不可避免的趋势，将话题引向硬件架构的发展。
• [ivolimmen] 提出能否在LibreOffice下运行Windows的问题，探讨了跨平台运行的可行性。
• [valorzard] 询问同样的技术是否适用于LibreOffice Calc，关注跨软件的兼容性。
• [goodboyjojo] 提到Linux和Doom常常是黑客首先尝试在设备上运行的程序，暗示了对技术挑战的兴趣。
• [padde] 询问实际的应用场景，例如能否通过Excel单元格与Linux用户空间互动，关注实际应用中的技术整合。

Linux In Excel
Linux running in Excel
How?
It makes use of
mini-rv32ima
.
The emulator is built as a seperate dll which is loaded by the VBA macro. The VBA macro calls the emulator in the dll and gets the output and writes it into the cells in the spreadsheet.
The thing is evidently very buggy but I did not want to spend a lot of time on it. This was done mostly for fun. Evidently this was cheating since I did not rewrite the emulator in VBA or Excel formulas but again I wanted to run Linux in Excel and this was one way to do so.
Building and Running
I was using MSVC to build the dll.
Use the following command
cl dllmain.c /LD /Fefun.dll
Then in the Excel file change the path to the dll.

43832662.article_content:
Mission Impossible: Managing AI Agents in the Real World
David Bethune
Follow
35 min read
·
6 days ago
--
2
Listen
Share
We are at a new frontier with AI tools in every industry, and particularly in software development. They are changing underneath us faster than any human can adapt, and charging us for the privilege. Maintaining control of these robots feels like an impossible mission. Today I’ll share some battle-tested techniques that you can use to rein in your AI agents, chats, and other tools.
This article is part of my
AI Library
. If you’re new to agentic coding, start with
License to Kill
. To dig deep into why and how this stuff works the way it does, check out
Something from Nothing
.
License to Kill: Coding with Cursor AI Agents
Cursor, an AI code writing and editing tool, represents a significant advance in the practical use of artificial…
levelup.gitconnected.com
Something From Nothing
A Painless Approach to Understanding AI
levelup.gitconnected.com
Your Mission
After many successes and failures I’ve had with AI agents, the mission comes down to careful planning and restraining the context of what your agents can do.
Everything that can be done wrong, I’ve done wrong.
If you can set the right guidelines, agents can deliver better results. Everything than can be done wrong, I’ve done wrong and learned from it. It should be no surprise that agents write software this way. Humans do, too, and that’s where agents get their ideas.
Choosing Your Tools
Choosing What to Work On
Finding a Route
Making a Plan
Revising the Plan
Testing the Plan
Finding Bigger Problems
Making Rules
Performance Payback
Choosing Models
Cost Controls
Model Context Protocol (MCP)
Fair Warning:
All screenshots and UI mentions are likely to be outdated by the time you read this, owing to how fast these tools change. The concepts will be there in different parts of the app if you hunt around.
Wheatfield with Crows
is my favorite Van Gogh painting. It’s stunning in person and
can’t be reproduced
in any medium. Oil paint impasto reflects photons into your eye in ways that aren’t duplicated by ink on paper or by emissive screens. In the same way, the materials and techniques in your existing code and your prompts determine the true qualities of the finished app.
1. Tools Are Not Materials, Nor Technique
Choosing Your Tools
I’m putting this issue here not because it’s the most important but because folks
think
it is. In art, there is a great difference between
tools, materials,
and
technique
. When the work is done, only the materials remain, transformed as they were by your tools and technique.
When you work with AI tools, the materials are your inputs — your code, diagrams, data, and prompts. The technique is how you weave these materials together and the order in which you present them. You’ll find a recurring theme throughout this article: the quality of the materials you provide will be the single most important factor in your AI agent’s success.
My examples will be from
Cursor
but I want to emphasize that the tool
du jour
has very little impact on what you can do, just like all washing machines have similar functions but different buttons.
AI tools change
daily
. If you haven’t updated yours today, it’s probably behind. The trick is to find the tool that offers a workflow that you like — one that offers a balance of investigation and action and boosts your own workflow.
You can apply everything I’ll talk about in Cursor with tools like
Windsurf
,
Copilot
for VS Code, or even by pasting stuff into ChatGPT or Google Gemini. You can also use all of these tools for free but, as with everything in life, the paid version is significantly better, so don’t judge the paid version of something by the free results.
Will non-devs create high quality output with these tools?
Absolutely not.
It’s also important to know your tool deeply and keep up with its
changelog
and documentation. I know no one reads that anymore but, ironically, in the age of “ask an AI anything,” the user of such an AI would do well to read the doc directly as the true secrets of its power are revealed only in the pages of those cryptic tomes.
Know Thyself
When working with AI, you must be realistic about your own abilities and shortcomings, for they will permeate everything the agent builds for you. When is it time to
investigate
, and when is the time to take
action
? You have to be the one to know and control that flow.
With AI tools, different skills pay the bills. Does that mean that non-devs (or non-artists) will create high quality output with these tools?
Absolutely not
. It means just the opposite.
In addition to your standard set of coding skills, you’ll need deep architectural insights and an ability to communicate them in plain English. That’s not a skill set that’s common among programmers. Don’t be upset at the LLM when its output is just as bad as your input.

Forget Me Nots
fame, remi

43807245.article_content:

The lost secrets of webOS
LG is about to unveil the future of webOS — but there’s a past we never saw
by
Dieter Bohn
Jan 2, 2014, 5:28 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
lost webos 1 lead
Next week,
LG will unveil new televisions running webOS
, the ill-fated operating system
it acquired in last February
. Although LG is
expected to retain some form of webOS’ interface
, exactly what that will mean on a television instead of a phone or tablet is still a mystery. If LG has any luck at all, it will be more successful than the last consumer webOS products. It’s been over two years since HP’s TouchPad and the Pre 3 were released and then discontinued in a surprise decision from then-CEO Léo Apotheker. In fact, most people within HP were blindsided when executives decided to stop hardware production and left the software team twisting in the winds of uncertainty. Apotheker’s decision ultimately led to the open sourcing of some parts of webOS and the sale of the rest to LG under current CEO Meg Whitman.
But back in 2011, before and after Apotheker’s fateful decision, Palm had been actively working on both new hardware and new software.
The Verge
has obtained documents describing Palm’s plans and even a design prototype of a new smartphone. They tell a story of a company struggling to innovate in the face of daunting competition and perishingly few resources. They also show that, even at the end, Palm’s ambition outstretched its ability.
This is the webOS that never was.
Embark
On February 9th, 2011, Palm's Jon Rubinstein took to the stage to unveil the first major products to come out of the division since the HP sale. The Pre 3 and Veer phones weren't much better than the Pre phones that came before them, but the TouchPad showed promise, at least on the software side. Unbeknownst to Rubinstein and his staff, the event — known internally as "Embark" — would be the high point of Palm's brief tenure at HP.
But the good vibes from the event didn't last long. Apple announced the iPad 2 on March 2nd, less than one month later and well before Palm's TouchPad was released. Though webOS on the TouchPad had some clever features and an elegant software design, the TouchPad itself was a hulking, plastic monster. It was for all intents and purposes a glossy black look-alike of the original iPad.
Apple's iPad 2 was as much of a revelation as the original iPad. It was radically thinner, lighter, and faster than what had come before and it immediately made the TouchPad — not to mention competing Android tablets — look stale by comparison. Apple released the iPad 2 to consumers just over a week after it was announced, while the TouchPad wasn't released until July.
Sapphire
If the documents we obtained detailing HP's product plans are any indication, the iPad 2 sent the company into a panic. In a document distributed in late March, HP admitted that the iPad 2 had "changed the competitive trajectory" and foresaw rapid responses from Samsung — which had shaved over 2mm from its Galaxy Tab tablet in response to the iPad 2. HP had also gotten pushback from the likes of AT&T, which wasn't happy with the TouchPad's "thickness, weight, [and industrial design]."
HP created a plan to refresh the TouchPad with the "Sapphire" (the TouchPad's codename was Topaz, and the Sapphire was also referred to as the "Topaz2"), with the unrealistic goal of developing it in "record time" and releasing it in late 2011. At the same time, it was working on another tablet that would feature a high resolution screen to be released in the latter half of 2012. The former would have brought the company to some kind of parity with Apple (albeit a year late), while the latter would have arrived a few months after Apple introduced a Retina display iPad. It also planned to work on a successor to the "Opal," the 7-inch tablet that was nearly released as the TouchPad Go before it was canceled.
HP's tablet plans looked reactionary in both specs and design. It was caught flat-footed by Apple and was rushing to make its traditional tablets competitive. It’s not clear how far along HP got with any of these plans, but it seems unlikely that any of them would have made their ship-date targets.
Mako
HP was also painfully aware that though the Palm faithful still liked hardware keyboards and the slide-out design of the Pre (and even the Veer), the rest of the world was moving to touchscreen-only phones. It had developed a version of the Pre 3 that had no physical keyboard, codenamed "
WindsorNot
." The WindsorNot was meant for AT&T but didn’t have LTE, and it was delayed past the point when AT&T would require all smartphones to have LTE.
However, HP was also working on a significantly more advanced phone, codenamed "Mako."
The Verge
obtained a design prototype of the device that reveals a new design direction eschewing the soft, nature-inspired pebble look of the Pre for something much more angular. It was to have a glass front and back, wireless charging, LTE, and a

data.title: Firefly's rocket suffers one of the strangest launch failures we've ever seen
data.author: divbzero
data.article_summary: Firefly Aerospace launched its Alpha rocket from California, but the mission failed after a mishap during first-stage separation. About two-and-a-half minutes into the flight, an issue occurred as the first-stage booster separated from the upper stage, resulting in a visible explosion-like event. The upper stage's engine, though ignited, lost its nozzle, significantly reducing thrust. Despite reaching an altitude of 200 miles (320 kilometers), the rocket failed to achieve orbital velocity. The payload, a satellite by Lockheed Martin, and the rocket ultimately fell into the Pacific Ocean. Firefly is investigating the cause with its partners and the FAA. This failure echoes past rocket launch anomalies, such as SpaceX's Falcon 1 incident in 2008.

Firefly Aerospace launched its two-stage Alpha rocket from California early Tuesday, but something went wrong about two-and-a-half minutes into the flight, rendering the rocket unable to deploy an experimental satellite into orbit for Lockheed Martin.
The Alpha rocket took off from Vandenberg Space Force Base about 140 miles northwest of Los Angeles at 6:37 am PDT (9:37 am EDT; 13:37 UTC), one day after Firefly called off a launch attempt due to a technical problem with ground support equipment.
Everything appeared to go well with the rocket's first-stage booster, powered by four kerosene-fueled Reaver engines, as the launcher ascended through fog and arced on a southerly trajectory over the Pacific Ocean. The booster stage jettisoned from Alpha's upper stage two-and-a-half minutes after liftoff, and that's when things went awry.
A blast from below
A bright cloud of white vapor appeared high in the sky, indicating an explosion, or something close to it. A moment later, the upper stage's single Lightning engine ignited for a six-minute burn to accelerate into orbit.
A ground-based infrared camera caught a glimpse of debris in the wake of the upper stage, and then Firefly's live video stream switched to a camera onboard the rocket. The rear-facing view showed the Lightning engine stripped of its exhaust nozzle but still firing. Shards of debris were visible behind the rocket, but the video did not show any sign of the discarded first stage booster, which was expected to fall into the Pacific south of Vandenberg.
The upper stage engine kept firing for more than six minutes, when it shut down and Firefly announced that the rocket reached orbit. The rocket was programmed to release its single payload, a nearly 2-ton technology demonstration satellite built by Lockheed Martin, approximately 13 minutes into the mission. Firefly ended its live webcast of the launch before confirming separation of the satellite.
A short time later, Firefly released a statement acknowledging a "mishap during first stage separation... that impacted the Stage 2 Lightning engine nozzle." As a result, the rocket achieved an orbit lower than its target altitude, Firefly said. The privately held Texas-based launch company amended its statement later Tuesday morning to remove the clause about the lower-than-planned orbit.
Another update from Firefly early Tuesday afternoon confirmed the launch failed. The company said the rocket "experienced a mishap between stage separation and second stage ignition that led to the loss of the Lightning engine nozzle extension, substantially reducing the engine’s thrust."
The launcher reached an altitude of nearly 200 miles (320 kilometers) but did not reach orbital velocity, according to Firefly.
"The stage and payload have now safely impacted the Pacific Ocean in a cleared zone north of Antarctica," Firefly said. "Firefly recognizes the hard work that went into payload development and would like to thank our mission partners at Lockheed Martin for their continued support. The team is working closely with our customers and the FAA to conduct an investigation and determine root cause of the anomaly."
While Firefly's live video of the launch lacked a clear, stable view of first-stage separation, the appearance of white vapor is a sign that the rocket was likely emitting propellant. It wasn't immediately obvious whether the first stage recontacted the upper stage after separation or if the booster exploded and harmed the upper stage engine.
You can watch a replay of Firefly's stage separation below.
Whatever the case, it's an interesting mode of failure. Maybe it's not as bizarre as
Astra's sideways launch
in 2021, something every rocket geek should know about. Also,
there's the time Astra's upper stage
launched itself through a half-open payload fairing in 2022. United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket
lost a nozzle
from one of its solid rocket boosters on a test flight last year, but the launch vehicle persevered and continued its climb into orbit.
The
third flight of SpaceX's Falcon 1 rocket
failed in 2008 when its first stage collided with its upper stage moments after separation. An investigation determined residual thrust after shutdown of the first-stage engine pushed the booster into the bottom of Falcon 1's upper stage, so SpaceX lengthened the time between main engine cutoff and staging. SpaceX's next flight was successful, making Falcon 1 the first privately developed liquid-fueled rocket to reach orbit.
The only time a rocket's first stage has exploded after separation, at least in recent memory, was in 2023, when a
North Korean booster blew up
before it fell into the sea. The explosion did not damage the rocket's upper stage, which continued into orbit on North Korea's only successful satellite launch in nearly a decade. The incident fueled speculation that N

data.title: Millions of Apple Airplay-Enabled Devices Can Be Hacked via Wi-Fi
data.author: agent86
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了苹果AirPlay功能中新发现的安全漏洞——被称为“AirBorne”。这些漏洞可能让黑客通过同一Wi-Fi网络入侵支持AirPlay的设备，如扬声器、电视等，传播恶意代码。尽管苹果已为自家设备发布补丁，但许多第三方设备可能多年得不到修复，因为它们的制造商很少提供更新。这些漏洞可能让黑客控制设备、窃听或将其加入僵尸网络。尤其在智能家居和车载CarPlay系统中，风险较大。尽管攻击需要在同一Wi-Fi网络内进行，且数据泄露有限，但仍存在潜在威胁。研究公司Oligo已向苹果报告问题并协助修复，但警告许多第三方设备仍可能长期存在漏洞。
